titleText.es: Según oigo, muchos de vosotros ya tenéis Flash fluido, pero yo y mi tarjeta Intel seguimos esperando un parche del kernel en algún punto de la pipeline para poder ver a Jon Stewart con fluidez.
titleText.en: I hear many of you finally have smooth Flash support, but me and my Intel card are still waiting on a kernel patch somewhere in the pipeline before we can watch Jon Stewart smoothly.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official xkcd source both identify comic #619. The archive translates the official title text while retaining the product and platform names Flash and Intel.

regions.labelEs: COSTÓ MUCHO TRABAJO, PERO ESTE ÚLTIMO PARCHE DE LINUX AÑADE SOPORTE PARA MÁQUINAS CON 4096 PROCESADORES, DESDE EL ANTIGUO LÍMITE DE 1024.

excludedUnits.rationale: 4096 is a processor-count numeral rather than a Spanish lexical word.
1024 is the earlier-limit numeral rather than a Spanish lexical word.

applications.explanationEn: Costó places the difficulty in completed past time, mucho strengthens the amount, and trabajo names the effort involved.
Último comes before parche and uses masculine singular -o to match it; here it identifies the most recent patch.
Soporte names technical compatibility, para introduces what is supported, and máquinas fills that device slot.

regions.labelEs: ¿TENÉIS YA SOPORTE PARA REPRODUCIR VÍDEOS FLASH A PANTALLA COMPLETA DE FORMA FLUIDA?

applications.explanationEn: The -éis ending marks the several people addressed informally in the vosotros form used mainly in Spain.
In this question about an expected feature, ya asks whether it is available yet or by now.
Soporte names compatibility, para introduces the supported action, and reproducir remains in its unchanged dictionary form.
A begins the fixed display expression, pantalla names the screen, and completa says that the whole screen is used.
Completa follows the noun pantalla in the ordinary descriptive order.
Completa uses feminine singular -a to match the feminine singular noun pantalla.
De forma introduces how the playback happens, and fluida describes that manner while matching the feminine noun forma.
Fluida follows the noun forma in the ordinary descriptive order.
Fluida uses feminine singular -a to match the feminine singular noun forma.
Quién carries a written accent because it directly asks which person.

cards.noteEn: Costó is a completed-past form of costar. With me, te, le, nos, os, or les, it can describe how difficult something was for that person rather than its price.

example.es: Nos costó terminar a tiempo.
example.en: It was hard for us to finish on time.

cards.questionEn: How can you say that doing something is difficult or takes effort?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of costar followed by trabajo; mucho can emphasize the amount of effort.
cards.noteEn: Costar changes for the time and for what is difficult: cuesta trabajo now and costó trabajo for a completed past situation. A person affected can appear with me, te, le, nos, os, or les.

example.es: Nos cuesta mucho trabajo organizarlo.
example.en: Organizing it takes us a lot of effort.

cards.noteEn: Trabajo often means work or a job. In costar trabajo, it instead names the effort or difficulty involved in doing something.

example.es: Aprender esta técnica cuesta trabajo.

cards.noteEn: Before a noun, último can mean the final or last remaining one, or simply the most recent one. The surrounding noun and situation distinguish those readings: el último superviviente is the last survivor, while mi último trabajo can mean my latest work.

example.es: Leí su último artículo.

cards.promptEs: número ordinal antes de un sustantivo
cards.questionEn: How do you use words such as first, second, or third before a Spanish noun?
cards.answerEn: Put the ordinal before the noun and make its ending match the noun's gender and number.
cards.noteEn: An ordinal gives a position in an order. Primero, segundo, tercero, último, and similar words usually come before the noun. Most forms use -o with a masculine singular noun and -a with a feminine singular noun, but primero and tercero shorten to primer and tercer before a masculine singular noun. Plural nouns use plural forms.

example.es: La segunda puerta está en el tercer piso.
example.en: The second door is on the third floor.

cards.noteEn: In computing, a parche is a small software update intended to correct a defect or security weakness.

example.es: Instalaron un parche para corregir el fallo.
example.en: They installed a patch to fix the flaw.

cards.promptEs: Linux · miles de procesadores · vídeo Flash fluido
cards.questionEn: What contrast creates the joke about the patch's supported features?
cards.answerEn: The patch supports an unusually specialized machine with thousands of processors, yet the user still cannot smoothly play ordinary full-screen Flash video. The developer celebrates impressive large-scale engineering while dismissing the everyday feature the other person actually wants.
cards.noteEn: Linux is an operating-system family. Flash was a widely used web-media platform when the comic appeared in 2009, and smooth video playback depended on practical graphics, driver, and software support rather than merely accepting a huge processor count.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links an item to its type
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between an item and the noun that identifies its type. English often puts the type noun first instead: libro de historia becomes “history book.”

example.es: Compré un libro de historia.

cards.answerEn: support; technical ability to work with something
cards.noteEn: In technology, soporte can mean that a system is compatible with a device, format, or feature, not only help from a support worker.

example.es: El navegador tiene soporte para este formato.

cards.questionEn: How do you name the device, format, feature, or action that a system supports?
cards.answerEn: Use soporte para, then name the supported thing or use an action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: A noun can follow para, as in soporte para impresoras. For a supported action, use an unchanged -ar, -er, or -ir verb: soporte para imprimir.

example.es: El programa añade soporte para cámaras nuevas.
example.en: The program adds support for new cameras.

cards.answerEn: for; introduces what technical support covers or enables
cards.noteEn: After soporte, para can introduce a device, format, feature, or action that the system can work with.

example.es: La aplicación incluye soporte para exportar audio.
example.en: The application includes support for exporting audio.

cards.noteEn: In computing, a procesador is the hardware that carries out program instructions. Procesadores is plural.

example.es: El servidor utiliza varios procesadores.

cards.noteEn: Before a noun, antiguo often means former or previous rather than physically old.

example.es: Rechazaron el antiguo sistema.

cards.noteEn: A límite can be a boundary or the greatest allowed value. In technical descriptions, it often names the maximum a system supports.

example.es: El límite del sistema es de cien usuarios.
example.en: The system limit is one hundred users.

cards.answerEn: you all have (informal plural, mainly Spain)
cards.noteEn: Tenéis is the present form of tener for vosotros or vosotras. It informally addresses more than one person and is used especially in Spain.

example.es: ¿Tenéis las entradas?
example.en: Do you all have the tickets?

cards.questionEn: How does Spanish in Spain address several people informally?
cards.answerEn: Use vosotros or vosotras forms, such as vuestro for “your” and podéis for “you all can.”
cards.noteEn: Vosotros addresses a mixed or all-male group; vosotras addresses an all-female group. These forms are common in Spain. Most of Latin America uses ustedes instead, with different verb and possessive forms.

example.es: Vosotras podéis traer vuestros libros.
example.en: You all can bring your books.

cards.noteEn: Ya often means ‘already.’ In a question about an expected change, natural English commonly uses ‘yet’ or ‘by now.’

example.es: ¿Ya funciona la impresora?

cards.answerEn: to play; to play back audio or video
cards.noteEn: With audio or video, reproducir means to play the media. In other settings it can mean to reproduce, copy, or recreate something.

example.es: Pulsa aquí para reproducir el vídeo.
example.en: Press here to play the video.

cards.noteEn: Vídeos is the plural of vídeo. The form with stress on ví- is standard in Spain; video without the written accent is common in much of Latin America.

example.es: Guardé los vídeos en el ordenador.
example.en: I saved the videos on the computer.

cards.noteEn: Flash is the unchanged name of an older multimedia platform. In a phrase such as juegos Flash, it identifies the technology used to make or run the games.

example.es: El museo conserva una animación Flash.
example.en: The museum preserves a Flash animation.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins a pantalla completa, ‘full-screen’
cards.noteEn: The display expression uses a before pantalla completa. Translate the complete expression rather than a by itself.

example.es: Abrió el mapa a pantalla completa.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that content is displayed using the whole screen?
cards.noteEn: Pantalla is feminine, so completa uses feminine singular -a. The preposition a remains fixed in this display expression.

example.es: Vimos la película a pantalla completa.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.

example.es: Necesito una mochila nueva.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.noteEn: In pantalla completa, completa matches the feminine singular noun pantalla and says that the content uses the whole screen.

example.es: La presentación está a pantalla completa.

cards.answerEn: in (as part of de forma, in a … way)

cards.questionEn: How can you express “in a ... way” by using forma?
cards.answerEn: Use de forma, then an adjective that describes that way of doing something.
cards.noteEn: Forma is a feminine noun, so an adjective with separate masculine and feminine forms uses its feminine form here: clara, rápida, cuidadosa. Adjectives such as normal that have one form for both genders do not change.

example.es: Respondió de forma clara.

cards.noteEn: Fluida describes something that moves or works without interruptions. In de forma fluida, it matches the feminine noun forma while the full expression describes how an action happens.

example.es: La animación se reproduce de forma fluida.

cards.answerEn: Write qué, cómo, cuándo, and similar words with an accent when they ask a question or add an exclamation.
cards.noteEn: This includes direct questions (¿Qué quieres?), questions inside another sentence (No sé qué quiere), and exclamations (¡Qué bonito!). Without the accent, these words usually connect parts of a sentence instead: el libro que quiero means “the book that I want.”
cards.questionEn: Why do words such as que, como, and cuando sometimes have a written accent?

example.es: ¿Cómo te llamas?

cards.noteEn: Usa is the present form of usar used for one third-person subject. It can also be an informal positive command meaning “use,” but that is not this sense.

example.es: La máquina usa poca energía.
